title: Crispy Lemon Lamb Breast Ribs
imagePrompt: Individual lamb rib strips are deeply browned with almost blackened edges, their surfaces crackling and rendered so the fat is translucent and the exposed meat is a rich mahogany. The bone ends poke out from each piece, and the cut faces show a layered cross-section of crisped fat and dark, tender meat. Scattered cilantro leaves rest on top, and the whole plate carries a faint golden sheen from the lemon juice and olive oil that has pooled slightly beneath the ribs.
subtitle: Slow-rendered at 300°F, then blasted hot for crisp edges. Built to serve with tzatziki + roasted potatoes.

ingredients.heading: Ingredients (Lamb)
ingredients.note: Built for rib-style pieces with lemon brightness to keep it from feeling heavy.
items: 1 split lamb breast plate (about 2.5–3.5 lb), cut into 1–2 slabs
Kosher salt (about 1½ tbsp total, adjust to size)
Black pepper (about 1 tsp)
Dried oregano (about 1 tsp)
Rosemary (1 tbsp chopped fresh or 1 tsp dried)
Garlic (3–5 cloves, grated or very finely minced)
Lemon zest (from 1 lemon)
Fresh lemon juice (2–4 tbsp, for crisp phase + finishing)
Olive oil (optional, 1 tbsp for rubbing / crisp assist)
ingredients.callout: Pairing: tzatziki + lamb-fat roasted potatoes. (You already proved this combo is dangerous.)

body.html: Lamb breast is rich (pork-belly energy). The trick is to render the fat slowly, then crisp the cut surfaces at high heat so it tastes bold—not greasy.

items: Mise en place — prep the herb-garlic rub, lemon, and roasting setup
Slow roast 300°F until soft & jiggly
Rest so it slices clean
Slice into ribs and blast at 475°F for crisp edges
Finish with lemon to cut richness

body.html: Serving vibe: rib-style pieces + tzatziki + roasted potatoes. Lemon is the balance lever.

items: Wash and dry the lemon and fresh rosemary, if using.
Chop 1 tbsp rosemary, grate or finely mince the 3–5 garlic cloves, and zest the lemon.
Measure the salt, pepper, oregano, rosemary, garlic, and lemon zest for the rub.
Juice the lemon and measure 2–4 tbsp; keep it separate for the crisp and finishing phases.
Pat the lamb breast plate very dry and set out the optional 1 tbsp olive oil.
Fit a wire rack over a sheet pan; gather paper towels, a sharp knife, and foil.

body.html: Hold the lemon juice: The zest belongs in the rub, but the juice is saved for the high-heat crisp and final finish.

items: Lightly score the fat in a crosshatch (don't worry if it's a bit deep—this cut is forgiving).
Rub with: kosher salt, black pepper, oregano, rosemary, grated garlic, and lemon zest.

body.html: Tip: Fat needs more salt than lean meat. If in doubt, add a light extra pinch on the fat side.
Place lamb on a rack and rest uncovered in the fridge if you can. Even 30–60 minutes helps the surface dry for better crisp later.
No time? Skip this and proceed—your crisp phase still works.

items: Preheat oven to 300°F.
Place lamb fat-side up on a rack over a sheet pan (uncovered).
Roast 2.5–3 hours (two pieces may finish a little sooner).

body.html:
Doneness cue: it should feel soft & jiggly. If using a thermometer, aim ~185–195°F.

If browning too fast: loosely tent with foil (don't seal—avoid steaming).
Remove from oven and rest 20–45 minutes. This firms everything up so you can slice clean rib-style pieces.
Good news: this cut can rest longer (even an hour) without drama—especially since you'll re-crisp it.

slides.title: Slice Into Ribs
slides.checkboxLabel: Flip bone-side up & slice between ribs

items: Flip the slab bone-side up.
Slice into rib strips between bones/cartilage.
Lay pieces on the rack with space between (more airflow = more crisp).

body.html: Optional crisp boost: lightly blot cut faces with a paper towel before the blast.

items: Raise oven to 475°F.
Lightly brush or drizzle ribs with lemon juice (don't soak).
Roast 15–20 minutes until edges are deeply browned and crisp.

body.html: Want more? Broil 2–3 minutes at the end for extra char—watch closely.

items: Immediately squeeze fresh lemon over the ribs.
Sprinkle a pinch of salt (flaky if you have it).
Scatter chopped cilantro (or parsley if available).
Serve with tzatziki on the side (dip, don't drown).

body.html: Balance rule: If it tastes "too rich," add more lemon—not more salt.
